summary: Mokurai Shimaji (1838–1911) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He held posts at Nishi Hongan-ji, Hongan-ji, and Gankyo-ji, and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen (Chiyoda Girls' Academy).

Mona Schrempf is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned her doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was attested as a research fellow at Berlin and a teacher at Heidelberg.

Monica Esposito (1962–2011) was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied at Venice, Fudan, Ghent, Paris Diderot, and the Sorbonne, and was appointed an associate professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

Monier Monier-Williams (1819–1899) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit from 1860 to 1887.

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies who completed her doctorate at the Free University of Berlin under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow. She later held professorships at Bonn, Cologne, Bamberg, and Heidelberg (1990–2006).

Monika Zin (born 1957) is an Indologist and art historian who completed her degrees at Jagiellonian University and the University of Munich. She has held professorships at Munich, Free University of Berlin, and the University of Leipzig.
Moodeen Sheriff (died 1891) was an Indologist who studied at Madras Medical College. He served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Tohoku University and Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman. He served as a professor at Sendai National College of Technology and later led Hosen Gakuen College.

Moritz Abraham Stern (1807–1894) was a linguist who studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen under Karl Otfried Müller. He served at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884, succeeding Carl Friedrich Gauss in 1858.

Moriz Haupt (1808–1874) was a German philologist who studied at the University of Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He was a professor at Leipzig (1841–1851) and Berlin (1853), and served as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1861–1874).

Moriz Winternitz (1863–1937) was an Indologist who studied at Vienna and under Georg Bühler and Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at Oxford and Visva-Bharati, and served as a professor of Indian philology at the German University in Prague from 1902 to 1934.

Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Copenhagen and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He has held teaching posts at Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler (1890–1976) was an archaeologist who studied at University College London. He served as director of the National Museum Wales and the London Museum, and was Director-General of Archæology in India from 1944 to 1948.
Morton Klass (1927–2001) was an anthropologist and Indologist who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He taught at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.
Mother Sayamagyi (1925–2017) was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. A disciple of U Ba Khin, she later succeeded him.

Motohiro Yoritomi (1945–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his degrees at Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He was a professor at Shuchiin University and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Motoi Ono (born 1958) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Yasunori Ejima, at the University of Tsukuba, and at the University of Vienna. He was appointed associate professor at the University of Tsukuba around 1999.

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held academic posts as a professor at Vidyasagar College in the 1970s and later in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He later held academic posts at the University of Leipzig and the University of Heidelberg.

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as Deputy Director of Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums (Andhra Pradesh), and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University.
